- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.2) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 3–7% to match true decline.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 3–5 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price moving away from 30-day moving average, model tends to overcorrect; align forecast toward historical mean or 30-day MA.
- Sentiment volatility >0.4 in last 5 days correlates with forecast error; dampen forecast volatility by smoothing with 3-day moving average or reducing standard deviation by 20–30%.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) price movements; increase forecast by 2–5% for final 7–10 days if sentiment is positive or neutral.
